The Supreme Court found that Hill misrepresented information to the trial court to engineer the removal of a juror she believed favored the defense. That's not a clerk who made some careless comments. That's a clerk who allegedly manufactured evidence to change the composition of a jury on the most important morning of the trial.
So why would a county clerk of court do this? Well, the easy answer is the book. And that answer isn't necessarily wrong. It's just incomplete.

Rhonda McLevin, the Barnwell County clerk who helped Hill during the trial, testified on her oath at the January 24 hearing that Hill had been talking about writing a book as early as December 2022, a full month before jury selection even began. McLevin said Hill told her that they should write it together because she needed a lake house and I needed to retire.

Makele even testified that during the trial, Hill brought up multiple times that a guilty verdict would sell more books. Hill denied it, but the Supreme Court didn't believe Hill's denials. The justices noted that Hill's conduct was consistent with her stated desire to sell more copies of her book. Even Judge Jean Toll, who initially denied the new trial motion, concluded Hill was not completely credible, but had been attracted by the siren call of celebrity. Remember that?

And the timeline makes it clear this wasn't a fleeting thought that got out of hand in November of 2022. Before the trial started, Hill emailed a French reporter who was writing a Murdoch book saying she was interested in writing her own, asking about a partnership. And during the trial itself, Hill emailed that off the record, we have a wonderful jury here.

After the guilty verdict, the media blitz accelerated. She emailed a producer for Nancy Gray seeking a book promotion interview. She coordinated with documentary crews from Netflix and Fox Nation for courthouse access. She earned what she testified was roughly $100,000 from sales of the book. before it was pulled from publication, after she was caught plagiarizing. She was indicted for using her public office to promote the book. She pled guilty to misconduct in office for exactly that.
